summary: Winning OCT specimen mask: "texture markers + rim watershed" (candidate g). Volume 18.05 cm3 at 0.15 mm (5,347,436 voxels, fraction 0.487, 1.36x the MRI tissue volume of 13.32 cm3) and 18.06 cm3 at 0.04 mm (282,254,507 voxels, fraction 0.484); one connected component; keeps 61.5% of the old intensity mask (28.86 cm3, 2.17x MRI). Boundary follows the visible bright specimen rim on all lateral surfaces at both resolutions (final_mask150.png / final_mask04.png); the remaining excess (~4-5 cm3) sits in artefact-rich agarose (the striped "comb" band under the ventral surface, striped tile pockets at the deep end) plus a few small exterior islands inside smooth tissue that connect to the x cut faces. Why the simple candidates fail on this dataset: (1) the embedding agarose is scatterer-doped, so its intensity equals tissue (medians 17.4-19.4k vs 16.4k) and the 3D local std at 0.15 mm is identical inside tissue and agarose (793 vs 714-931); only the specimen surface (rim, 3-5k) differs; (2) the rim is incomplete: the deep-end (large z) boundary of the brainstem has no rim at all (interface parallel to the section plane; shortest non-rim path from the box centre to the z-end face never exceeds local std 1793 < rim threshold 3408), and the 0.04-mm rim max-pooled to 0.16 mm still leaves the interior and agarose as one component even after 0.48 mm opening; (3) the specimen is cut by both x faces of the box and touches the black tiles at tile edges, so neither the faces nor the zero region can seed an exterior flood (zero-seeded floods give 30 cm3 = everything or 3-5 cm3 = leak). What does separate agarose from tissue: agarose artefacts are anisotropic (x tile stripes, per-section z sawtooth) but quiet along y, while tissue texture is isotropic; the min-over-axes directional std (normalised by local mean) computed at 0.04 mm after a 0.08 mm band-pass gives agarose 124 vs tissue 433 (86% of agarose reference below the tissue 5th percentile). That field gives markers; a watershed on the 0.04-mm rim strength snaps the boundary to the rim where one exists. Candidates measured (cm3 at 0.15 mm): (a) fine texture alone: Otsu 4.6 (threshold lands on the rim class), log-GMM 17.15 (mincv) / 14.26 (minstd, interior holes); (b) gradient + exterior flood 2.35 / 4.17 (leaks); (c) local std 0.75/1.05 mm + Otsu + close + fill 4.19 / 4.69, extfill 4.39 / 4.93 (rim shell only); (d) min/max anisotropy ratio at 0.15 mm 15.6-16.6 (ragged, clean agarose looks isotropic); (e) min-axis std/CV at 0.15 mm + log-GMM 13.4 / 15.7, with rim watershed 10.8 / 13.8; (f) 0.15-mm rim watershed with 0.04 texture markers 17.2-18.1; (g, final) 18.05. Fallback rule triggers here: 28.86 / 13.32 = 2.17 > 1.5.
recipe:
Option "--oct-mask texture" for prep_subject.py (CPU, 4 processes, ~4 min for a 728x1006x797 octv; peak RAM < 20 GB). Inputs: octv.npy (0.04 mm, float16, slab-normalised, zeros = missing tiles), octv_affine, the oct150 grid + affine, V_mri = mri_tissue volume. Reference implementation: work/probe_xr/mask/scripts/{p1_aniso04.py (step 1), p1_rim04.py (step 3), p1_final.py (steps 2,4-7), p1_common.py (cleanup)}.
1. Texture field at 0.16 mm (p1_aniso04.py). Process octv in z-chunks of 128 slices (+16 pad) with multiprocessing.Pool(4): m = (octv>0); bs = G_sigma2[octv*m] / max(G_sigma2[m],1e-3) with sigma = 2 vox = 0.08 mm (band-pass: removes speckle); for each axis a in (z,y,x): masked 1D running std with window w = 9 vox = 0.36 mm: mu_a = U_w(bs*m)/U_w(m), s_a = sqrt(max(U_w(bs*bs*m)/U_w(m) - mu_a^2, 0)), set s_a = 0 where U_w(m) < 0.5; local mean MU = U_9(bs*m)/U_9(m) (3D window 9); weighted mean-pool by 4 of (s_z*m, s_y*m, s_x*m, MU*m, m) -> 0.16 mm grid (182x251x199), affine = pooled_affine(octv_affine, 4); divide by pooled m; valid = pooled m > 0.5; masked Gaussian smoothing sigma = 3 cells = 0.48 mm on each; F = min(s_z, s_y, s_x) / max(MU, 1); F = 0 outside valid.
2. Threshold: 2-component 1-D Gaussian-mixture EM on log(F[valid & F>0]) (subsample to 500k, 100 iterations, init means at the 25th/75th percentiles, equal sd = std/2); thr = exp of the point between the two means where the weighted component densities are equal. (Here thr = 0.01514; GMM log-means -4.47 / -3.75, sd 0.44 / 0.56, weights 0.41 / 0.59.) Do NOT use Otsu / multi-Otsu on this field: they split at the rim class (4.6 cm3) or too low (20 cm3).
3. Rim strength at 0.16 mm (p1_rim04.py): per chunk at 0.04 mm, 3D local std with window 5 vox (0.2 mm), Gaussian sigma 1 vox; max-pool by 4 -> E (elevation); E = 0 outside valid. (The Otsu threshold of this map, 5084, is only needed for the diagnostic rim fraction: 10.3% of voxels.)
4. Markers: inner = binary_opening(F > thr, ball r = 4 cells = 0.64 mm); outer = binary_opening(F < thr, ball 4) OR ~valid. Watershed (skimage.segmentation.watershed(E, markers)); specimen = (label == inner) & valid. Marker scale factors > 1 (stricter inner markers) drop real smooth tissue and are not recommended.
5. Enclosed exterior pockets: label the exterior (label == outer & valid); components that touch no box face and no zero cell (1-cell dilation of ~valid) are reassigned to the specimen.
6. Cleanup at 0.16 mm: closing with ball r = 3 cells (0.48 mm) on an edge-padded array (np.pad mode='edge'; plain scipy binary_closing erodes the specimen where it is cut by the box faces), largest connected component, binary_fill_holes.
7. Resample: mask16 as float -> map_coordinates(order=1, mode='nearest') through inv(A16) @ A_target onto the 0.15 grid, > 0.5, AND oct150 > 0, then largest CC + fill holes -> oct150_mask; onto the 0.04 grid in 64-slice chunks into an open_memmap bool file, > 0.5 AND octv > 0 -> octv_mask.
8. Fallback rule: compute the intensity mask as now (oct_tissue_mask); if V_intensity > 1.5 x V_mri_tissue, replace oct150_mask / octv_mask by the texture masks (here 28.86 > 1.5 x 13.32 = 19.97 -> texture used, giving 18.05 cm3); record both volumes, thr and the GMM parameters in prep.json. Parameters (all in mm): band-pass sigma 0.08, directional std window 0.36, pooled grid 0.16, field smoothing 0.48, rim window 0.20, marker opening radius 0.64, closing radius 0.48. Only "thr" is data-driven (GMM).
numbers: Targets: MRI tissue 26,005,914 voxels at 0.08 mm = 13.315 cm3 = 3,945,193 voxels at 0.15 mm = 208.0 M voxels at 0.04 mm; MRI tissue mapped into the OCT box via T_oct2mri = 12.62 cm3 (MRI box covers 73.2% of the OCT box). Old intensity mask: 8,551,247 voxels, 28.86 cm3, fraction 0.779, 2.17x MRI; OCT box 37.06 cm3; zero (missing-tile) voxels 19.0% of the box, one connected component reaching all six faces. Final mask (g_ws16_open4_scale1.0_close3): 0.15 mm: 5,347,436 voxels, 18.048 cm3, fraction 0.487, ratio to MRI 1.355, 1 CC, keeps 0.615 of the old mask, 1.65% of it lies outside the old mask; 0.16 mm working grid 18.06 cm3; 0.04 mm: 282,254,507 voxels, 18.064 cm3, fraction 0.484. Versus MRI-in-OCT via T (pose-limited): recall 0.725, Dice 0.597, 43.4% of the mask inside the MRI-covered region is outside MRI tissue (old mask: recall 0.913, excess 49.1%); missed MRI tissue 3.5 cm3 lies in visibly agarose regions of the OCT (pose residual >= 3-5 mm, largest along z). Separability (medians, 0.15 mm, window 1.05 mm, smoothing 0.45 mm; tissue = 22-voxel ball at box centre, agarose = imaged voxels at z<11 or z>188): intensity 16.7k vs 19.4k; 3D local std (0.45 mm) 876 vs 1932 (agarose has more!); std_z 788 vs 2813; std_x 840 vs 745; std_y 846 vs 407 (80.5% of agarose below tissue p5); min/max anisotropy 0.9 vs 0.14. At 0.04 mm (band-pass 0.08 mm, window 0.36 mm, smoothing 0.32 mm): std_y 433 vs 124 (86.3% of agarose below tissue p5), 3D lstd 711 vs 690 (no contrast), std_x 429 vs 565, std_z 308 vs 325. Rim at 0.15 mm: Otsu of smoothed local std (w=0.45 mm) 3408 (w=0.75 mm: 4177, w=1.05 mm: 4744); shortest non-rim path from box centre (97,133,106) to the z-end face (193,208,106): 196 steps, max local std 1793 (no rim crossing). Rim at 0.04 mm (w=0.2 mm): Otsu 5084, 10.3% of voxels; after max-pooling to 0.16 mm the non-rim space stays one component: 26.0 cm3 (r=0), 19.2 (opening r=2), 15.4 (r=3) with 28k face-contact cells. Candidate volumes at 0.15 mm (cm3): b_grad_extfill dil0/dil1 2.35 / 4.17; c_lstd5 close2_fill 4.19, extfill 4.39; c_lstd7 close2_fill 4.69, extfill 4.93; zero-seeded floods 30.03 or 3.4-5.2; d_aniso w5/7/9 x sig2/3/4 15.6-16.6; e_minstd_w7_sig3 Otsu 5.55, log-GMM 13.43 (ws 10.75); e_mincv_w7_sig3 Otsu 4.73, log-GMM 15.73 (ws 13.84), multi-Otsu 20.9; a04_mincv_bp2_w9_sig3 Otsu 4.59, log-GMM 17.15 (ws 16.56), multi-Otsu 19.75; a04_minstd_bp2_w9_sig3 log-GMM 14.26; f_ws_lstd3 open3/4/5 band1.0 17.76 / 17.88 / 18.07; g_ws16 open3/4/6 x scale1.0 17.47 / 17.90 / 18.42, scale1.5 13.34 / 13.77 / 14.84 (drop real tissue), scale2.0 9.4-9.9; final with pocket fix + edge-padded closing 18.05. Runtime (4 CPU processes, OMP 4): texture field 79 s, rim field 34 s, watershed + cleanup + both resamplings ~95 s.
caveats: (1) The final mask is 1.36x the MRI tissue volume, not ~1.0x. The excess is agarose with strong sectioning artefacts: the striped "comb" band directly under the brainstem's ventral surface (adjacent to the cerebellum piece), striped tile pockets near the deep end and along the top tiles, plus a few exterior islands inside smooth tissue that stay because they connect to the x cut faces through smooth tissue. No candidate drops these without also dropping real smooth interior tissue (marker scale 1.5 -> 13.8 cm3 but with holes in the pons). The "13.3 cm3" target itself is uncertain: the MRI crop covers only 73% of the OCT box, so part of the OCT specimen may lie outside the MRI field of view. (2) All MRI-based numbers (recall 0.73, Dice 0.60, excess 0.43) are dominated by the current pose, not by the mask: the MRI tissue mapped through T_oct2mri lands in visibly agarose regions of the OCT (missed_g_ws16_open4.png), with displacements of >= 3-5 mm, largest along the sectioning axis; the old mask's recall of 0.91 only reflects that it is a superset. Visual boundary agreement at the rim is the criterion I trust. (3) The deep-end (large z) surface of the brainstem produces no rim in OCT (interface parallel to the section plane; no intensity contrast against the scatterer-doped agarose), so the mask boundary there is texture-only and uncertain by ~1-2 mm; this is the same region where the registration residual is largest. (4) The specimen is cut by both x faces of the OCT box and touches the black tiles at tile edges, so any recipe that seeds an exterior flood from the box faces or from the zero region will leak; the recipe relies on the watershed + pocket rule instead. Plain scipy binary_closing / binary_fill_holes also misbehave here (face erosion, open cut faces). (5) The GMM threshold is data-driven and the two log-classes overlap (agarose reference has a long tail); the agarose reference region (first imaged sections) is atypically quiet, so the separation percentages are optimistic. Otsu-type thresholds on the texture field fail on this data. (6) Assumptions for other subjects: zeros mark missing data; specimen surface is bright at 0.04 mm on lateral faces; agarose artefacts are quiet along at least one array axis. Scatterer-doped agarose makes intensity useless, which is why the intensity mask fails. (7) Recommended second pass once a coarse pose exists: markers from the eroded/dilated MRI tissue via T (e.g. +-2 mm band) with the same rim watershed would remove the fringe/deep-end excess; not implemented. (8) The sklearn module is absent in the octmri env; the GMM is a 30-line numpy EM in p1_final.py.
